None for respondent No.2.
 Order

This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS/ 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 419/2023 registered at Police Station - Bandri, District Sagar (M.P). for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(3), 376(2)(cha), 506 of IPC and sections 3, 4, 5(N), 5 J (ii) of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 20.11.2023.

First application was dismissed as withdrawn and second bail application was dismissed on merits.
2.

As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that on 01.02.2023 when prosecutrix was sleeping in her house around 8.00 PM he entered into house and committed rape upon the minor prosecutrix.
After investigation, offence under the aforesaid section has been registered against the applicant and co-accused.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 20.11.2023.
He has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is submitted that DNA NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-JBP:55404 2 MCRC-47163-2024 report does not support the prosecution story.
Prosecutrix's statement was recorded before the trial Court in which she has not supported the prosecution story.
In this regard, counsel for the applicant sought attention of this Court in paragraph Nos. 8 to 10 of the prosecutrix's statement.
Charge sheet has been filed.
Applicant has no criminal past and conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that present applicant is brother-in-law (jija) of the prosecutrix.

It is submitted that Bharat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71450036/
1 applicant has committed rape upon the minor prosecutrix and co-accused has also committed rape upon the prosecutrix due to which she got pregnant and delivered a child.

entities.text: Bharat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: DNA report of the child matched with the co-accused person but prosecutrix in paragraph No.1 of the Court statement of the prosecutrix has specifically stated that present applicant has committed rape upon her many times in absence of her parents.
His earlier (second) bail application was dismissed by a reasoned order and there is no change in circumstances of this case.
Therefore, it is prayed for dismissal of bail application.

5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, looking to the entire allegation levelled against the applicant and seriousness of offence, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
6. Accordingly, the bail application is hereby dismissed.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE shahina Bharat vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71450036/
